The king of Judah
A prophet of Israel

A desire to rebuild the city

One of Ben-hadad’s servants
A prophet

The elders of the land

Drinking himself drunk in the pavilions
Fleeing toward Aphek

answers: Seven thousand
Two hundred and thirty-two
One hundred thousand

He did not know Israel was in the city
He was drunk and was not prepared for the attack

Every soldier left the battle
Each soldier guarded his own tent

To announce that the Lord would give Israel the victory
To appoint the kings of Syria

The kings went out first
The young men went first, followed by the main army

He escaped on a horse with the horsemen
He immediately surrendered to Ahab

Israel had more horses
easy.explanation: They said that Israel’s God was a God of the hills, where Israel had been stronger.
easy.q: How did Ben-hadad’s servants explain Syria’s first defeat?

answers: Samaria
Damascus
Aphek

It was rebuilt immediately
It stopped Israel’s army

They proposed returning the army to Samaria

answers: Horses
Military leaders or commanders
Prisoners

Israel had lost Samaria
Ben-hadad did not come to the battle

Israel was mounted, while Syria fought on foot
Israel was in the city, while Syria was at sea

In the Israelite camp
In the hills of Samaria

Sackcloth on their loins and ropes upon their heads
Royal garments

My servant

To make Ahab king of Syria

answers: In the garments of a king
With ashes upon his face
In sackcloth and ropes
easy.explanation: The prophet disguised himself with ashes upon his face.
easy.q: How did the prophet disguise himself?

answers: Strike him
Bring him a horse
Guard the king
easy.explanation: The prophet said to the man, “Smite me, I pray thee.”
easy.q: What did the prophet ask the first man he met to do?

easy.explanation: Ahab went to his house heavy and displeased and came to Samaria.
easy.q: Where did Ahab go after the prophet rebuked him?

answers: A lion slew him
He became king
He fled to Damascus
medium.explanation: The prophet warned him, and after he departed, a lion found and slew him.
medium.q: What happened to the man who refused to strike the prophet?

answers: The man’s life would be required for the prisoner’s life, or he would pay a talent of silver
The man would receive a reward
The man would be sent to Samaria
medium.explanation: Ahab’s judgment was that the guardian would pay with his life or with a talent of silver if the prisoner were missing.
medium.q: What judgment did Ahab pronounce in the prophet’s story?

answers: You concealed the matter
You have pronounced the judgment yourself
You forgot the case
medium.explanation: Ahab declared that the man had determined his own sentence by his own words.
medium.q: What does Ahab’s statement, “Thyself hast decided it,” mean?

answers: It reflects Ahab’s release of Ben-hadad, a prisoner who should have been kept

It explains Israel’s first victory
challenge.explanation: The parable led Ahab to judge the release of a prisoner, and the prophet then applied that judgment to Ahab’s release of Ben-hadad.
challenge.q: How does the prophet’s parable relate to Ahab’s action?

answers: To make Ahab judge the case without knowing it was a parable
To escape from Syria
To ask Ahab for a covenant
challenge.explanation: By disguising himself, the prophet caused Ahab to pronounce judgment on a situation resembling his own.
challenge.q: Why did the prophet conceal his identity at first?

answers: Ahab had refused to go to war
Ahab had let go a man whom the Lord appointed to destruction
Ahab had failed to consult the elders
challenge.explanation: The prophet rebuked Ahab for releasing Ben-hadad, whom the Lord had appointed to destruction.
challenge.q: What was the prophet’s central rebuke to Ahab?
